articles.title: Rod Stewart confirms final tour after heart procedure and health scares
articles.summary: Rod Stewart announced his "Final Encore Tour," revealing next year's dates will be his last-ever tour after a coronary stent procedure and health setbacks.
articles.body: Rod Stewart is ready for one final encore. The rock legend announced "The Final Encore Tour" Monday, revealing that next year will mark his last-ever tour after facing a series of health issues. "Well, here we go… one last time!" Stewart wrote on Instagram. "Come and see me on my The Final Encore Tour for one more round of rock ’n’ roll. I’m really looking forward to it." ROD STEWART CALLED 'TONE-DEAF' FOR ATTENDING WORLD CUP GAME A DAY CANCELING CONCERT DUE TO HEALTH ISSUES Stewart opened up about his decision to make the tour his last in an emotional video message. "Ladies and gentlemen, after much deliberation and sadness, I have to announce next year will be my last tour ever, ever, ever," he told fans. "I’m not retiring, but this will be the last rock and roll tour," he clarified. "I wanna thank you for everything you’ve given me, and hopefully I’ve given you something in return," Stewart said before singing, "Please come out and see me on the tour. It’s gonna be great!" In the comments, fans said they were "heartbroken" and thanked Stewart for his music. "Sir Rod, After 53 years and nearly 300 shows across four continents, I am heartbroken that I just have one more year of your AMAZING live shows. Can’t wait to see ALL of them. Thank you for a lifetime of music that created incredible moments and memories. You live will be missed," one fan wrote. "You have given me so much joy, a real good reason to travel the world and the chance to met wonderful people (some of whom I can call my friends now). Gratitude, Respect and Love forever," another wrote. Another fan added, "Love you Sir Rod!! Thank you for all the Rock N Roll you given all of us!!" "You have given us so much there are no words. Wishing you all the very best," one fan wrote. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Stewart has faced a string of health setbacks in recent years. He has canceled shows after battling strep throat, COVID-19 and the flu. His health troubles continued in 2026, when a sinus infection and an acute upper respiratory infection that led to laryngitis forced additional cancellations. In August, Stewart canceled the remaining dates of his "One Last Time Tour" after undergoing a coronary stent procedure. "Doctors are pleased with his recovery, and Rod is doing very well and has returned to his normal daily activities," Stewart's team shared on Instagram at the time. "On the advice of his doctors, he will take the next four weeks to recuperate and regain full fitness before returning to the stage." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "So, he’s on the cycling machine warming his legs up, he’s warming his voice up, he’s getting prepared with his outfit, it’s like pumping his chest, you know? And he comes out the dressing room, and it’s that walk down the corridor to his stage," she said during an appearance on the "At Home with Vanessa" podcast. "And once he gets onstage, he doesn’t just walk on, like he runs on. And the first song, it’s like go, go, go. And he does that for like an hour and a half, two hours." Lancaster said Stewart's demanding routine was why doctors wanted him to give his body time to heal. articles.title: Quote of the day by Matt Damon: ‘You have to engage and turn towards the problems that you see. Walk right up to them, look them in the eye, and then look yourself in the eye and decide what you're going to do about them’, 'The Martian actor’s words on how important it is to face your problems
articles.summary: Matt Damon's quote emphasizes the importance of facing your problems head-on rather than ignoring them. He encourages taking action and engaging with challenges to restore personal agency.
articles.body: Matt Damon has been through his own fair share of hardships in life. Today’s quote comes from an understanding that ignoring your problems or waiting for time to take care of them for you will never work. Instead, it is essential that you face them head-on and work towards your goal.The quote from ‘The Martian’ star Matt Damon reads, "Turn toward the problems you see. You have to engage and turn towards the problems that you see. Walk right up to them, look them in the eye, and then look yourself in the eye and decide what you're going to do about them.”What does the quote from Matt Damon mean?Damon had shared this piece of advice with students in June 2016, during the commencement speech to the graduating class at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). In the speech, Damon shared a piece of advice former President Bill Clinton had once given him ("turn toward the problems you see"), urging graduates to engage directly with real-world problems and embrace failure as a learning experience.The meaning behind the quote lies in understanding that human nature often leads people to look away from overwhelming issues. However, when you directly approach the problem head-on, it means that you are choosing to push past barriers and you are choosing to engage over being apathetic. Other than that, "walking right up" and looking a problem "in the eye" in the quote means directly confronting the reality of a situation and the fear that you are feeling directly rather than letting your emotions and thoughts magnify it. By examining an obstacle up close, you can take away its ability and power over you and help you understand the situation better.The quote is also about understanding your own capabilities and how you have to come to terms with your abilities. “Looking yourself in the eye” means that you confront all parts of yourself and understand how you are going to face your problems from now on. Lastly, the ultimate goal of turning toward a problem isn't just to feel concerned; it's to make a decision and take action. Even if your contribution resolves only a fraction of a massive issue, making a conscious choice to act restores your agency in the matter.About Matt Damon’s early lifeMatthew Paige Damon was born on October 8, 1970, in Cambridge, Massachusetts. His father, Kent Telfer Damon, was a stockbroker and tax preparer, while his mother, Nancy Carlsson-Paige, was a professor of early childhood education at Lesley University. His parents divorced when he was a child, and he and his brother moved to Cambridge to live with their mother afterwards. Damon then went on to study at the Cambridge Rindge and Latin School, which is a public high school located in Cambridge. During his time here, Damon developed an inkling for theater and acting, and he started working on school plays regularly. Not only that, but it was his drama teacher, Gerry Speca, who helped him hone his skills and encouraged him to pursue acting more seriously in life.When he was a teenager, Damon met Ben Affleck, and the two became close friends and have remained so. Since both of them wanted to pursue acting, they started working together, traveled together to auditions in New York, and went on to collaborate on various projects. In 1988, Damon started attending Harvard University for his degree in English literature. He continued to take part in school plays and even scored minor roles in films. It was here that he first wrote the script for ‘Good Will Hunting’ for an English assignment. Around the same time, he made his official debut in ‘Mystic Pizza.'In 1992, Damon was just shy of 12 credits from graduating from his class; however, he still dropped out and dove headfirst into the world of acting. He and Affleck refined the ‘Good Will Hunting’ script and pitched it everywhere they could, with only one request: that they were going to star in the film itself. After facing a lot of rejections, the two finally got the film made, and it is still one of the most popular films from their career.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 1994, Jack Nicholson donated 60 acres of Los Angeles land that could have become four homes; decades later, it remains protected habitat
articles.summary: Discover how Jack Nicholson's anonymous 1994 donation of 60 acres of land in Los Angeles has preserved vital natural habitat and prevented luxury home development, ensuring wildlife thrives in the Santa Monica Mountains.
articles.body: Veteran icon Jack Nicholson, who is best known for his work in ‘The Shining,' once donated around 60 acres of land that was originally under his name. The actor has taken the underdeveloped land located in Coldwater Canyon to the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy back in 1994.The plot, located near Franklin Canyon, had already received city approval for subdivision into four luxury home sites, which would have netted millions on the open market. However, Nicholson still donated the land to the conservatory to save the green, neighboring forest. Not only that but at the time, the veteran icon made the donation anonymously.Jack Nicholson donated a 60-acre plot in 1994 anonymouslyThe Los Angeles Times reported at the time that someone had made a donation of 60 acres of land to the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy. However, at the time, no one knew who the donor was since everything had been done anonymously, and there was no way to track down the person behind the donation. The land had native oak woodland and deer habitat on it, and the conservancy had been buying out additional pockets of land in the same area to help maintain a continuous stretch of wild habitat located between Griffith Park to the east and Topanga State Park to the west.At first no one knew it was Nicholson who made the hefty donation; however, after verifying some internal sources, multiple officials, including John A. Diaz (then the land-acquisition chief for the Conservancy), all confirmed that the icon had made the donation personally. However, at the time, Jack’s manager had declined to issue any official comments about the matter.What happened to the 60-acre land that Jack Nicholson donated?Had the pre-approved lots been built there instead of the clear stretch of land that still thrives, this would have been one of Los Angeles's most expensive real estate stretches. According to reports shared online, the property to date has become a major part of the stretch that helps conserve an important portion of the mountains' new Mudholland Drive. The property is now filled with native oak woodlands, chaparral, and natural habitat that supports local fauna like mule deer, bobcats, coyotes, and various bird species.It was unclear for a long time as to who had made the donations, especially since Nicholson’s business manager had refused to make any comments about the matter. According to another report published later on by The Times, Turnley Walker, who was the chairman of the Longridge-Alomar Neighborhood Committee at the time, revealed that Nicholson was the donor. The land was referred to as a Nicholson donation.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'SNL' host Michael Che mocks Macklemore's 'Free Palestine Tour' after Ed Sheeran drops rapper
articles.summary: Michael Che mocked Macklemore's "Free Palestine Tour" on "Weekend Update" after the rapper was dropped from Ed Sheeran's U.S. stadium concerts.
articles.body: "Saturday Night Live" comedian Michael Che mocked rapper Macklemore during "Weekend Update" on Saturday night in New York City over his newly announced "Free Palestine Tour," which came after the rapper was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. stadium tour following his pro-Palestinian performances earlier this month. Che set up the joke by noting Macklemore’s removal from Sheeran’s tour before turning to the rapper’s new slate of concerts. "Rapper Macklemore, who was dropped as the opening act for Ed Sheeran, announced that he is launching a Free Palestine tour," Che said. "But haven’t the Palestinian people been through enough?" he asked. BILL MAHER HAMMERS MACKLEMORE OVER GAZA REMARKS, HIGHLIGHTS RAPPER'S CONTROVERSIAL 'JEW' COSTUME FROM 2014 Christian Toto, an award-winning film critic, journalist and founder of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital that celebrity commentary about the Israel-Palestinian conflict often follows what he described as a socially rewarded position within the entertainment industry. "There is only one acceptable answer for celebrities when it comes to the ongoing Israel-Palestinian conflict. Say 'Free Palestine' and nothing else. It's the new BLM, a contentious issue where celebrities know they'll gain approval within their circle by repeating that mantra. They also understand they won't be pressured to defend their point of view by the vast majority of entertainment reporters. It's a safe space for them," Toto said. "Journalists now know they can pepper stars with similar questions and get a similar response (and lots of clicks for their interviews)," he continued. FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE Macklemore announced the "Free Palestine Tour" on Thursday, with shows scheduled for Dublin on Oct. 26, Paris on Oct. 29 and London on Oct. 30. Additional performers and U.S. dates were expected to be announced later, while proceeds will benefit organizations supporting Palestinians, according to the rapper. In announcing the tour, Macklemore argued that artists could no longer remain outside the debate over the war in Gaza. "It’s 2026. Being apolitical during a genocide doesn’t work anymore," Macklemore said. "People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it." MS RACHEL URGES 'EVERY WEALTHY WHITE CELEBRITY' TO MATCH MACKLEMORE'S DONATION TO PALESTINIAN CAUSES The announcement followed weeks of controversy after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his protest song "Hind's Hall" while opening for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4 and 5. The Messina Touring Group said multiple upcoming venues would not permit concerts to take place with Macklemore on the lineup. Sheeran later stressed that he was not personally responsible for removing Macklemore and said he had attempted to resolve the dispute before the venues and promoter made their decision. Fox News Digital reported that Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga subsequently withdrew from Sheeran’s tour in solidarity with Macklemore. "Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine," Sheeran said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Macklemore said he would donate the $1 million he earned from Sheeran's tour to organizations providing aid to Palestinians. Sheeran and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft also announced plans for $2 million contributions toward humanitarian relief in the region. When asked whether increasingly political performances risk turning entertainment into a litmus test for performers and audiences, Toto said he believes most musicians remain cautious about alienating concertgoers. "Most artists know better than to alienate audiences with their political views. The Springsteens, Morellos and Macklemores remain the exception. Concert ticket prices are too high for most bands to get on their soapbox and risk dooming repeat business," Toto told Fox News Digital. "Actors don't make the connection between their divisive words and audience reaction. They simply want to appease their fellow actors and make nice with potential directors and casting directors. So they read from the approved script." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Kraft, Sheeran and Macklemore for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: Actor Robert Davi swapped LA’s homelessness and crime for Florida skies
articles.summary: Actor/singer Robert Davi swapped LA’s escalating homelessness, crime and failed leadership for the Sunshine state
articles.body: While veteran actor, singer and filmmaker Robert Davi has long been an outspoken critic of California’s political leadership, its current policies and Hollywood’s cultural direction, he never really saw himself leaving the Golden State. The 75-year-old character actor, known for playing iconic tough guys in films like "The Goonies" and "Die Hard," as well as a James Bond villain in "License to Kill," may have been born and raised in a tight-knit Italian family in Queens, New York but Los Angeles became his adopted home in 1977. Like many others before and after him, he headed west to the Golden State when his on-screen career began to take off, and he grew accustomed to the California lifestyle. ZACHARY LEVI CALLS CALIFORNIA A ‘FAILED STATE’ THAT IS ‘LITERALLY AND FIGURATIVELY ON FIRE’ AFTER TEXAS MOVE But for Davi, who has also been vocal about what he sees as a political blacklist in Hollywood because of his support for President Donald Trump, there were multiple breaking points that he said ultimately led him to sell his home and leave the state for Florida. This January will mark four years since he and his family joined other Californians who left for the Sunshine State. "The overwhelming influx of homelessness in all communities, the political corruption and the waste of money by the local education agencies in Los Angeles that’s not used for students but for administration costs, and most of that goes to the political party of their choice, and the mismanagement of the LA fires were all [contributing] factors," Davi told Fox News Digital. HOMEOWNERS IN LEAFY ENCLAVES HIT BY BURGLARS ZEROING IN ON HIGH-END HOMES FOR SMASH-AND-GRAB SCORES "When I first came to LA, I could go to CVS and it was fine. I could go to a store. It was fine. Now they have gates, they have guards and items are behind lock and key because of the rampant crime," Davi added, noting, "It’s about people coming in and the acceptable aspect of going into any store and ripping off what they want and not being stopped." Still, like many who fall in love with California’s weather and relaxed lifestyle, Davi hung on to the home he loved, hoping what he saw as rising crime and political dysfunction might somehow improve. But it was the Dec. 1, 2021, home invasion and killing of Jacqueline Avant — the wife of Grammy-winning music executive Clarence Avant — at her Beverly Hills home that became the last straw for Davi. The 81-year-old was the mother of Alexander Avant and Nicole Avant, the former U.S. ambassador to the Bahamas and wife of Netflix co-CEO and chief content officer, Ted Sarandos. KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS "Why did I leave California? It was knowing this and watching this happen. It was the nail in my coffin," Davi said. "California was seeping into this s---, the crime that was happening within communities and continually encroaching into communities … a home invasion and murder by a criminal that was let go three different times?" A classically trained singer in both opera and traditional pop and jazz, Davi is known for performing the music of his idol, Frank Sinatra. He is also closely associated with Hollywood’s music community, strongly supports teaching musical instruments in schools and was close to the late record producer and composer Quincy Jones. Jones, in turn, was close with Clarence Avant. For Davi, the incident resonated deeply. Within months, he and his family moved out of the state. Davi wondered about what he considers a key question: how did California and Hollywood, in particular, get so left-wing? Davi recalled the days when Ronald Reagan was running for president, noting how hard those in Hollywood were on the actor-turned-politician at the time, but how conservatives didn’t have to hide their beliefs back then. Davi played Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev in the 2024 biopic "Reagan," which was re-released in theaters on Sept. 25. "The Screen Actors Guild (SAG) wasn’t afraid. Conservatives were not afraid to talk. Johnny Carson was fair," Davi said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You had conservatives that were big stars that spoke out and you had liberals. Since that time, liberalism has taken on another form," he explained. Fox News Digital reached out to California Governor Gavin Newsom's office for comment.

"the Girls" will debut on Thursday, Oct. 1, with a premiere episode featuring FOX News Media stars Rachel Campos-Duffy, Harris Faulkner and Kat Timpf, newly named FOX News contributor Melissa DeRosa and former ESPN host Samantha Ponder. The personality-driven conversation series will feature an array of leading female voices with new episodes dropping every Thursday. 'RUTHLESS' HOSTS TRACK DOWN TOP REPUBLICANS AT RNC MIDTERM CONVENTION IN NEW FOX NATION SPECIAL Albano added, "We’re excited to deliver a no-holds-barred format that captures the authenticity and perspectives of the many dynamic women of FOX News Media and beyond."
